[LUNI.2.7.1] The compiler bakes `Rational`→`float64` conversions and the tier-2
build-time round-trip test ([§4.3]) using **round-to-nearest-even** (IEEE 754
`roundTiesToEven`) and a **fixed left-to-right evaluation order**. The same
`.ds` source therefore yields **byte-identical baked factors** in the emitted
`.dsc` on any IEEE-754-compliant build host — DSC reproducibility holds at the
unit-system layer.

Concretely: an affine factor `= <expr>` ([§4.3]) is folded as a Rational
operand-by-operand left-to-right, then a single `roundTiesToEven` cast to
`float64` produces the baked constant. A tier-2 `to_base`/`from_base` pair
applies the same `roundTiesToEven` rule to every intermediate `float64`
operation. No host-dependent transcendental enters the bake — irrational
factors (e.g. `year_tropical`, [§16.2]) are pre-rounded to their pinned
`int64`-ns constant at spec-authoring time and committed as such, never
re-derived from `float64` at build.

The device side carries the other half of the guarantee: a runtime **MUST**
use the baked constant as emitted and **MUST NOT** recompute the factor. A
tier-1 conversion is then `a·x + b` in correctly-rounded basic operations, and
so cross-platform bit-exact; recomputing the factor on-device forfeits that.
